Definition: from G1933; suitableness, i.e. (by implication) equity, mildness:--clemency, gentleness.
BiblicalUsage: Epieikeia is gentleness, equity, clemency — the reasonableness that does not press a case to the letter. Paul asks Felix to hear him of his clemency a few words, and beseeches the Corinthians by the meekness and gentleness of Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: Gentleness is not weakness but equity, I hold: the strength that knows when to press and when to forbear, after the pattern of Christ.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
